newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah firms, liquidity remains tight.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah firms, liquidity remains tight.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah firmed against the dollar in moderate late Friday trading on the back of sustained tight money market liquidity, dealers said.
They said the market focus was on liquidity supply which turned extremely tight due to higher than expected weekly tax payments and the end of the liquidity reporting period.
"This seemed to have caused a sharp jump in overnight money," one Japanese bank dealer said.
He said overnight money stabilised at 17 percent at midday as operators resorted to short-term securities (SBPUs) for some fresh funds, after hitting an early high of 26 percent.
But the overnight rate soared again to a new day's high of 36 percent as some banks emerged to borrow rupiah late in the afternoon after discovering some unmatched positions.
One foreign bank dealer said volume was thin and he expected the rate to stabilise on Monday, although operators were waiting for some clues from Tuesday weekly tax payments.
One said swap premiums gave mixed direction as operators unloaded longer-term swap rates but bid for short-dated swaps.
Spot rupiah was quoted at 2,323.0/24.0 at 0900 GMT against an opening of 2,325.5/26.5 to the dollar.
Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,322.70/23.00 and 2,321.0/22.0, respectively.
Overnight swap was at 2.75/2.90 and tom/next at 0.4/0.5.
One-month swap was quoted 15.25/16.50, two at 32.50/34.50, three at 47.50/48.75 and six at 97.50/98.25 points.
Dealers said sentiment remained firm on the rupiah after the central bank widened its intervention band on Wednesday to eight percent from five percent.
Bank Indonesia kept its intervention rate at 2,309/2,501 and the conversion rate at 2,309/2,357 on Friday.
